correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the equal-norm barycentric certificate: if c=sum w_i v_i (nonnegative w sum1) has <c,v_i>≥||c||², with equality on support, then radius²=2−||c||² is globally minimal and center unique by weighted variance identity. For k≥4 the two directed arms have Gram diagonal 2, neighboring −1, shared-source +1. The explicit quadratic arm weights sum 1/2 per arm and solve the discrete second-difference equations, yielding ||c||²=3(2k−1)/[(k−1)k(k²−k+1)]. The two omitted arcs have strict dot-product clearance giving 6(k²−4k+2)/[(k−1)k(k²−k+1)] for k≥4. k=3 separately has six positive weights and R²=28/17. Independent exact rational tests covered k=3,4,5,8,30 with all vertex distances and contacts; full result follows from symbolic all-k identities, not the tests.

The full published semi-balanced canonical-sphere theorem was separately inspected: it gives only an all-vertex sphere and a feasibility criterion, and explicitly leaves true smaller minimum sphere unspecified when infeasible, precisely this k≥4 case. The separate path one-reversal result concerns a tree and one excluded contact rather than a cycle and two. O passes best-of-knowledge with terminology risk.
